newsitem.title: USA: Stanley sets restructuring, cuts 4,500 jobs.
newsitem.headline: Stanley sets restructuring, cuts 4,500 jobs.

text.p: Tool and hardware maker The Stanley Works said Friday it will cut 4,500 jobs and reduce its manufacturing and distribution facilities to 70 from 123 as part of a restructuring.

The company plans to centralize its manufacturing, engineering, sales and service, finance, human resource and information technology operations. The savings from the shift will allow Stanley to focus on new product development, brand development, advertising and expansion into a number of related products, it said.

Stanley said it will record restructuring costs totalling $240 million, which includes $140 million of cash costs and $100 million non-cash costs. The company will record $137 million of the charges in the second quarter and the rest in the third quarter.

Stanley said 1997 second quarter earnings, before the effects of the restructuring, were 56 cents a share, up from 49 cents a share in the year-ago period. After the charges, Stanley reported a net loss of 72 cents a share, compared to a profit of 37 cents in the previous year.
"New products are the lifeblood of a manufacturing company," said Stanley chairman and chief executive John Triani.

"Increased expenditures will be made on new product development and expansion into a number of "near-neighbor" or related products," Triani said adding, "To support this thrust, we have established a corporate marketing and brand development function, whose focus will be the nurturing and leveraging of the Stanley brand."
